title: Agent memory and planning
description: Use scoped state and bounded plans without turning past text into authority.
objectives: Separate working state from durable memory
Design a plan with verification and stopping conditions
explanation: Working state holds information for the current task: the goal, observations, pending steps, and completed actions. Durable memory carries selected information across tasks. Persisting everything is rarely necessary; store provenance, owner, purpose, and expiry so later retrieval can apply the right scope.

A plan is a proposed sequence of actions, not evidence that the actions succeeded. Execute a bounded step, inspect the actual result, and update state. Keep authoritative action records outside generated summaries so a compressed conversation cannot turn a proposal into a completed transaction.

Checkpoint enough state to resume safely after interruption. Before retrying a step, check whether an external effect already occurred. Limit steps, elapsed time, and spending. Ask for missing information or stop with a clear result when progress is impossible; endlessly rewriting a plan is not progress.

terms.definition: Information needed for the current task execution.
Selected information retained across tasks or sessions.
Persisted execution state used to resume work.

example: A support agent remembers a user preference for short replies, but not access tokens. During a refund task it stores the proposed action, approval, and transaction identifier separately. A restart checks the transaction before considering a retry.
mistakes: Treating remembered text as verified policy.
Sharing memory between users without scoping.
Marking a step complete because it appears in a plan.
exercise: Design a three-step support workflow. For each state field, choose lifetime, owner, source, and deletion rule. Simulate a restart after the external action succeeds but before the final answer is sent.

questions.question: What distinguishes a plan from an execution record?
questions.answer: A plan proposes actions; a record documents observed actions and results.
questions.distractor: A generated plan proves all its steps are complete.

questions.question: What metadata helps control durable memory?
questions.answer: Owner, source, purpose, timestamps, and retention or expiry rules.
questions.distractor: Only the number of characters stored.

questions.question: A process restarts after a possible write. What should it do first?
questions.answer: Check the authoritative operation result or deduplication record before retrying.
questions.distractor: Repeat the write immediately without inspection.

questions.question: Why keep tool results separate from conversation summaries?
questions.answer: Summaries can omit or distort details needed to determine what actually happened.
questions.distractor: Generated summaries are stronger evidence than transaction records.

questions.question: What prevents an agent from looping indefinitely?
questions.answer: Enforced step, time, and resource limits with explicit stop conditions.
questions.distractor: A durable memory database by itself.
